How standard deviation is calculated

Population deviation divides the sum of squared deviations from the mean by n. Sample deviation divides by n−1, applying Bessel’s correction when the list represents a sample. For 2, 4, 6, the mean is 4; population SD is √(8/3) ≈ 1.633, while sample SD is 2.

Population σ=√[Σ(x−μ)²/n]; sample s=√[Σ(x−x̄)²/(n−1)].
A worked example

For 2, 4, 6, the mean is 4; population SD is √(8/3) ≈ 1.633, while sample SD is 2.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Which choice should I use for a sample?

Choose sample when these observations estimate a wider population.

Why does sample mode require two values?

With one observation, n−1 is zero and sample variance cannot be estimated.
